description.narrative: Access Now is seeking to strengthen human rights and democratic actors in the digital age while raising the importance of human rights, democracy and the principles of the rule of law. The intervention will contribute to more transparent and accountable democratic societies with a focus on countries in development, better enjoyment of human rights online for the most vulnerable and marginalized, an greater digital safety and security for actors and organisations working to uphold human rights. To achieve the overall goal Access Now work through their four interconnected arms technology, advocacy, RightsCon and the forwarded grants.

By working with digital rights and support for vulnerable journalists and activists, Access Now aims to strengthen human rights in the digital space, and reach people living in poverty as well as human rights defenders, and other vulnerable people such as women, girls and LGBTIQ groups.

Genom att arbeta med digitala rättigheter och support till utsatta journalister och aktivister vill Access Now stärka de mänskliga rättigheterna i det digitala rummet, och nå människor som lever i fattigdom samt människorättsförsvarare, och andra utsatta som till exempel kvinnor, flickor och HBTIQ grupper.

The 24/7 Digital Security Helpline has continued to provide direct digital security support to civil society activists and organizations. The team has handled more than 3,700 cases.
The Advocacy team successfully coordinated the #KeepItOn coalition to prevent internet shutdowns in several countries; launched and expanded 17 civil society-led campaigns; and successfully appealed to the U.S. Department of Treasury to amend its internet exemptions for global sanctions programs following years of sustained and dedicated advocacy.
Access Nows annual conference RightsCon convened more than 8,000 participants, both online and in person in San José, Costa Rica (June 5-8). The sessions predominantly focused on tactics and contexts for activists, online hate and violence, digital security for communities, and governance, politics, and elections.
The Grants program played a crucial role in supporting digital rights defenders awarding a total of just over $800,000 USD to 27 organizations across 17 countries, more than half of the grants made in 2023 went to organizations with an operating budget of less than $200,000.
